candidates.title: Batch Update of Mailing Address (staff screen)
candidates.user_story: As a Notice Processing Officer who needs to correct the contact and mailing address of an offender who is the current offender on many outstanding notices, I want to search all outstanding notices by the offender ID and update the offender particulars and mailing address on the selected notices in one action, so that letters for all those notices go to the right address without editing notice by notice.
acceptance: Menu entry 'Batch Update Mailing Address' opens the page /batch-update-odh

Search by offender ID returns only outstanding notices where that ID is the current offender (offender_indicator = 'Y'), excluding PS-FP and PS-PRA, and excluding other permanent suspensions except DIP, FOR, MID, RIP, RP2; the list is paginated
Officer picks notices, enters offender particulars (name, ID, phone, email) and address (postal code, block, street, floor, unit, building) and confirms
The same details are written to every selected notice; the processing stage is not changed
Officer can choose to also set the mailing address as the letter address (setAsLetterAddress)
Result lists success and failure per notice

evidence.what: Menu entry 'Batch Update Mailing Address' pointing to MetaBatchUpdateODH path
menu.push(LinkBatchUpdateODH) in the main menu

searchOutstandingNoticesByIdNo with the outstanding / not-permanently-suspended filters (Javadoc lines 725-737)

candidates.works_basis: Complete chain found: menu entry -> route -> UI call -> controller -> service -> DB update, and the endpoints are in api-authorization.properties. No environment flag found that switches it off. Which role sees the menu entry depends on LinkData(allowedUrls) at runtime; cannot verify from repo. No test was run.
candidates.ura_requested: no (no flow deck exists in repo); maintenance tickets do not mention it either
candidates.points_basis: Estimate only. Same size class as Batch Furnish OCMS41.50 (5) plus OCMS41.51 (5) taken together, but this screen reuses the furnish update code, so 8 instead of 10. MGG and URA decide.

candidates.title: Redirect current offender to an existing Owner/Hirer/Driver record on the notice
candidates.related_note: OCMS41.44-41.47 (all Demo paid) cover: check existing particulars, prompt them on screen, record/update particulars, confirm overwrite. None of them says that the officer can switch the current offender to another record that already exists on the notice (without keying new particulars), or that the stage, amount payable and admin fee are reset when this happens. That switch is the added scope.
candidates.user_story: As a Notice Processing Officer who finds that the person who should be followed up is already recorded on the notice as owner, hirer or driver, I want to redirect the notice to that existing record with one confirmation, so that the notice restarts the correct reminder flow against that person without re-keying the particulars.
acceptance: On the Owner, Hirer and Driver forms a Redirect button and a confirmation modal are shown when the particulars already exist but that person is not the current offender
On confirm the system finds the target record by notice number, owner/driver indicator and ID number, sets the old offender_indicator to 'N' and the target to 'Y'
UEN (ID type B or U) is refused as Driver

The processing stage is changed to the first stage of the new party (RD1 for owner/hirer, DN1 for driver), amount payable is recalculated from the composition amount and administration fee is set to 0
TS-HST is re-evaluated: revived if the old offender was in the HST list and the new one is not

evidence.what: RedirectBtn and RedirectConfirm modal exposed on the owner form (same on HirerForm.tsx:467 and DriverForm.tsx:453)

staffRedirect (Javadoc steps lines 304-318)

new stage, amount payable recalculation, administration fee set to zero
TS-HST revive when old offender was HST and new one is not
staff-redirect is in the authorization mapping

candidates.ura_requested: no (no flow deck exists in repo). Tickets OCMS-DF-2026-092/093 report on the HST side effect of this flow but do not request the redirect itself.
candidates.points_basis: Estimate only. Compared with OCMS41.46 (3) for record/update particulars plus the stage and amount reset logic, which is more than a single update story; 5 matches Batch Furnish OCMS41.50. MGG and URA decide.
demo_steps: Open a furnishable notice that has both an owner and a hirer record, where the owner is current

candidates.title: CAS inbound interface: push court notice updates and read payment status
candidates.related_note: OCMS27.23 (status blank) is about receiving warrant execution details (new court mention date, updated stages). The existing trace already credits only 'Sebagian' for this endpoint because the payload carries no warrant or mention-date data. The added scope is the general CAS interface: a batch push that overwrites stage, suspension, amount payable and payment-acceptance flag on court notices, and a batch read of payment status for CAS.
candidates.user_story: As a Court Processing Officer who works in the Court Administration System (CAS) for notices already in court, I want CAS to push stage, suspension, amount payable and payment-acceptance changes into OCMS and to read the current payment status of court notices from OCMS, so that OCMS and CAS show the same state and payment is only accepted when allowed.
acceptance: POST /v1/casUpdateCourtNotices accepts up to 500 notices; larger payloads are refused with a payload-too-large code
Each accepted notice has stage, suspension, amount_payable and payment_acceptance_allowed updated in the intranet VON and, when it exists, the internet eVON
A notice that is already paid (payment status FP) is rejected with the message 'Notice already Paid'
POST /v1/casGetPaymentStatus returns, per notice, suspension type, CRS/EPR reasons, payment status, amount payable, amount paid and payment acceptance flag, or a not-found code
Concurrent CAS calls are limited by a throttler that returns HTTP 429

evidence.what: POST /v1/casGetPaymentStatus with throttle check
POST /v1/casUpdateCourtNotices with throttle and 500-notice limit
getPaymentStatus reads VON and returns payment fields
updateCourtNotices
paid notices are rejected with 'Notice already Paid'
multi-row UPDATE per chunk (OCMS-DEV-2026-129 performance work)
both CAS paths skip the JWT filter
both CAS paths are excluded from the authorization interceptor
ocms.cas.key.validation.enabled=false

But the property ocms.cas.key.validation.enabled=false in prod (and dev) and a grep of the Java source finds no code that reads ocms.cas.key.validation, so the subscription-key check is not done in this repo. Whether CAS really calls these endpoints in UAT/prod, and whether APIM protects them, cannot be verified from the repo. Maintenance tickets that mention CAS (OCMS-SR-2026-164, OCMS-SR-2026-179) are data patches, not calls to this interface.
candidates.ura_requested: no (no flow deck exists in repo). Ticket OCMS-SR-2026-179 (On Hold) reports payment_acceptance_allowed stuck blank on court-stage notices, which is related data but not a request for this interface.
candidates.points_basis: Estimate only. Two endpoints with batch validation, throttling and a multi-row update to two databases; similar in size to OCMS22.23 (8, generate and interface court files). MGG and URA decide.
demo_steps: Call casGetPaymentStatus in UAT with 2 known notice numbers and 1 unknown one and check the three results
Call casUpdateCourtNotices for an unpaid court notice and check stage and amount_payable in VON and eVON
Call it again for a paid (FP) notice and check the 'Notice already Paid' result
risks: Orphan numbers #149, #153, #155, #162, #175, #243, #246 already list the same endpoints; the trace of OCMS27.23 already credits part of casUpdateCourtNotices as 'Sebagian'. This must not be claimed twice.

The endpoints skip JwtFilter and the authorization interceptor and the key check is off in prod properties: anyone who reaches the URL could change stage and amount payable if APIM does not protect it. URA may treat this as a defect, not a feature.
No evidence in the repo of an actual caller (CAS is external).

notes: All 71 seed leads were checked: they collapse into 6 candidates, the rest are in not_claimable. Many seed lines are the same feature seen by different agents (for example batch update address #150/#210, CAS #149/#153/#155/#162/#175/#243/#246, PLUS court reduction #110/#113/#115/#116, CPS #72/#102/#104/#105/#109, RIP #88/#89/#93, resubmission #198), so the parent should not add the orphan counts and the candidates together. Candidate strength order: Batch Update Mailing Address, RIP report, Redirect offender; CAS interface is Low confidence because of the security exposure and no proof of a caller. Status caveats: OCMS27.23, OCMS4.5 and OCMS46.x have a blank or 'No requirement' status in stories.json, so URA may still treat them as unbilled scope that includes my items. No flow deck or workbook exists, so ura_requested is 'no' everywhere; maintenance tickets only show URA used or fixed some of these features. Line numbers were read with grep -n and sed on the six repos on main; nothing was run or built. Role/menu visibility (LinkData allowedUrls, FUNCTION_ID.REPORT_RIP / REPORT_CPS) is decided at runtime and cannot be verified from the repo.
